summary: Closure review of a preregistered paired study comparing a verifier+bounded repair pipeline to accepting a single LLM candidate (shared_initial estimand). Execution, preregistration, analysis, and artifact archiving appear complete and internally consistent. The main outstanding problems are manuscript presentation defects: inline OpenAlex/archive URL tokens and extensive embedded file paths/hashes/provenance text remain in the main body instead of conventional scholarly citations and concise archival pointers. These presentation defects replicate the prior required revisions and are unresolved; they must be fixed before finalisation. Scientific design, execution, and primary inferential results are adequately supported by archived artifacts.
critical_issues: Manuscript still uses inline OpenAlex URLs and archive‑style tokens (e.g., https://openalex.org/…) in Related Work and body text rather than conventional scholarly citations and a formatted reference list; this violates the prior required revision and conference expectation for literature‑grounded prose.

Main body contains extensive inline file paths, repository paths, and artifact hashes (execution/model_configuration.json, execution/raw_results.jsonl, SHA‑256 values, etc.) that amount to provenance inventory in the narrative instead of concise scholarly exposition; this duplicates the previously requested condensation and relocation of low‑level provenance to the archived bundle.

Disclosure Statement, while present, repeats low‑level manifest entries and hashes inline rather than presenting a compact prose disclosure that cites the archived run bundle/manifest once; the manuscript must keep the Disclosure Statement concise and fully within the five‑page limit.
required_revisions: Replace every inline OpenAlex URL token and archive‑style link used as an in‑text citation with conventional IEEE‑style citations (numbered) and include properly formatted BibTeX entries drawn from the archived terminal_bibliographic_records. Use the verified terminal_bibliographic_records for all bibliographic metadata; do not leave OpenAlex links in the narrative.

Remove or substantially condense all inline file paths, raw artifact filenames, and full hash strings from the main body (text, figure captions, and tables). Instead add one concise sentence in Methods and in the Disclosure Statement pointing readers to the archived run bundle and manifest (provide the manifest path and a single representative manifest SHA‑256 once). Relocate the detailed provenance inventory (file paths, full hash manifest) to the archived artifact bundle; cite that bundle in the manuscript rather than embedding its contents.

Rewrite the Disclosure Statement as compact scholarly prose that still lists required items (models used, adapter/framework, master prompt reference, preregistration id and SHA‑256, high‑level execution summary such as planned/completed episode counts and model_calls_used) but does not enumerate low‑level file paths or hashes inline. Ensure the Disclosure Statement remains inside pages 1–5 and retains all required content items (use the archived manifest reference for low‑level proof).
optional_revisions: Consider adding a brief methodological justification for the paired bootstrap percentile CI choice given minimal discordance and/or include an exact bound alternative (artifacts for exact alternatives are archived).
Move the explicit note that the optional preregistration pilot was not executed earlier into Methods for clarity (the run already discloses this; placing it earlier improves reader comprehension).

Add a short paragraph in Discussion contrasting the shared_initial estimand with alternative estimands that permit resampling or iterative verifier‑guided regeneration, and briefly discuss tradeoffs between repair budget and model‑call cost using archived repair_stage_count/model_calls_used values.
Edit figure and table captions to remove any remaining provenance wording and ensure concise interpretive captions appropriate for IEEE two‑column format.
